thread:
Maria Lopez: Heads up — LinguaAI (pilot) sent a detailed ask: they want Optimize toolkit recommendations for a multilingual long-context workload. Key asks: per-language quantization guidance, runtime fallback to fp16 for critical routes, and eval-triggered alerts scoped by language and prompt set. They want a launch checklist for pilot by EOW.
Jon Patel: Good summary. Do we have telemetry to show per-lang quality delta post-quant? :thinking_face:
Devon Reed: We have coarse per-model evals but not per-language line-items. Could run targeted evals against their prompt set, should be doable if they share sample prompts.
Sara Nguyen: LinguaAI's constraint: some languages (e.g., Vietnamese, Arabic) show higher regressions when we push 4-bit quant. They want an automated fallback to a higher-precision variant for those traffic slices.
Maria Lopez: Exactly. Proposed scope for pilot: (1) run per-lang evals on their cust prompt corpus, (2) produce recommended quant profiles + confidence thresholds, (3) implement runtime policy to route to fp16 when eval confidence below threshold, (4) wire eval-triggered alerting to Ops/PM. Thoughts?
Jon Patel: Agree. For (3) we can reuse existing routing policy DSL but need a small extension: allow "language" predicate and per-route precision override. Example config snippet: ```policies:
- name: quant-fallback
  match: { language: "vi|ar|zh" }
  if: "model.quant.confidence < 0.85"
  then: { model_variant: "fp16" }
```
Devon Reed: That snippet looks fine. Caveat: adding language detection adds CPU overhead; for long-context requests detection must run early (first chunk). We should measure perf delta and include as acceptance criteria.
Sara Nguyen: Ops ask: also include a manual kill-switch and a rollout window (canary 1% -> 10% -> 100%) with rollback thresholds defined by per-lang eval metrics and latency regressions.
Maria Lopez: Launch checklist draft (brief): 1) LinguaAI prompt set ingested + sanitized; 2) per-lang eval run with baseline vs quant profiles; 3) policy DSL extension implemented + unit tests; 4) canary routing + perf monitor; 5) eval-triggered alerting flows to #support and PagerDuty; 6) customer sign-off on quality thresholds.
Jon Patel: Proposed acceptance metrics: per-language quality delta <= 1.5% BLEU-equivalent (or customer metric), p99 latency change <= +30ms, routing CPU overhead < 5%.
Devon Reed: I'll volunteer to own the eval runs and quantitative report. Need access to their prompt set and expected ground truth or scoring function.
Sara Nguyen: I'll own runbook + canary playbook. Will add PD escalation mapping.
Maria Lopez: I'll coordinate customer-facing thresholds and get sign-off. @prod-bot can you create tasks for owners?
prod-bot: Created tasks: #1234 eval runs (Devon), #1235 policy DSL (Jon), #1236 runbook + canary (Sara), #1237 customer sign-off (Maria). ETA EOW for initial eval artifacts. :white_check_mark:
Jon Patel: Quick question — do we want eval-triggered alerts to be "soft" (email + slack) first, then escalate to PD only after X regressions in 24h? Less noise for pilot.
Sara Nguyen: Yes — soft alerts -> triage -> escalate if persistent (configurable threshold). Add to runbook.
Maria Lopez: Great. I'll ping LinguaAI for prompt corpus and their preferred quality metric. Meeting if needed. Thanks team.
